sentences.text: Pinacosaurus was a lightly built, medium-sized ankylosaurine, a type of armored dinosaur, reaching about 5 meters in length and weighing up to 1.9 metric tons.

Its name, meaning "plank lizard," refers to the bone tiles protecting its head, while its neck, back, and tail were shielded by armor made of keeled osteoderms, which are bony plates embedded in the skin.

This animal used a smooth beak to bite low-growing plants, which were sliced by small teeth and processed in an enormous hind gut, likely aided by muscular tongues and tongue bones since its teeth grew slowly.
The type locality for Pinacosaurus hilwitnorum is the Djadochta Formation in Mongolia, where this newly described species was found.

Unlike many ankylosaurs preserved on their backs, most Pinacosaurus juveniles are found on their bellies in a resting position with legs tucked in, suggesting they were part of a traveling herd killed and buried by a sandstorm at Bayan Mandahu.
Pinacosaurus could actively defend itself using a tail club.
The genus Pinacosaurus was named by Gilmore in 1933. Originally placed in the Nodosauridae, it is now considered an ankylosaurid and a likely member of the Ankylosaurinae.

In 2026, Paul Penkalski transferred Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus to the genus Eopinacosaurus based on differences in the skull and cranial osteoderms, though Robert Hill considered Pinacosaurus mephistocephalus a valid species in 2012 based on secondary dermal horns and narial characteristics, though this status was later challenged.
In 1952, Maleev named a new ankylosaurid, Syrmosaurus viminicaudus, but it is now considered a junior synonym of P. grangeri.
Pinacosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous period, specifically in Mongolia and China during the Campanian stage, roughly 75 to 71 million years ago.
It inhabited a semi-desert habitat interspersed with oases.
Later research indicated that the sediments containing Pinacosaurus fossils at Alag Teeg were deposited during a flood, not a drying pool.
It is debated whether Heishansaurus pachycephalus is a valid species, as Arbour and Currie concluded in 2015 that it is a nomen dubium.
It is debated whether Pinacosaurus exhibited ant-eater-like insectivorous behavior.
The precise function of the nasal opening arrangement is unclear.
